notes.1: This question was generally well done. Most candidates realised that it was necessary to use Newton’s Second Law horizontally, and also to resolve vertically, in order to find the normal reaction and the friction force respectively. Answer: 0.556
notes.2: This question was quite well done. By using horizontal and vertical motion, u and u , the initial horizontal x y and vertical velocities could be found. If θ was the required angle, then tanθ=u /u , would give the correct y x answer. A few candidates found s and s , the horizontal and vertical distances. They then said x y tanθ=s /s which was an incorrect method. y x Answer: 77.3°
notes.3i: This part of the question was generally well done. Candidates needed to resolve vertically and to also use Newton’s Second Law horizontally.
notes.3iii: This part was not as well done. Too many candidates failed to realise that the reaction was zero. Answers: (i) 4.70 N (ii) 1.07
notes.4i: This part of the question was generally well done. Unfortunately a number of candidates did not obey the instructions given in the question. They just used the trajectory equation and substituted the known values into the equation.
notes.4iii: Most candidates substituted y = 5 into the given equation in part (i). Two values of x were found but these values were not subtracted in order to find the required distance. x 4x2 Answers: (i) y = − (ii) 32.5 m 3 375
notes.5i: This part of the question was not particularly well done. The first point that candidates needed to recognise was that zero acceleration occurred at the equilibrium position. The extension at this point was required. The candidates had to then set up a five term energy equation. Too often only four terms were seen.
notes.5iii: This part of the question proved to be far too difficult for many candidates. A three term energy equation was required starting at the point where the velocity was that found in part (i) up to the point where the velocity was zero. Answers: (i) 5 ms–1 (ii) 1.2 m
notes.6: Too many candidates tried to involve volumes in their moment equation. This was not necessary as the weights were given.
notes.6i: This part of the question could be solved by taking moments about O.
notes.6iii: Very few candidates were able to answer this part of the question. To do so candidates were required to take moments about the point of contact of the hemisphere and the rough surface. The required equation was 30×0.075sin60=P×0.4sin60. Answers: (i) 0.3 m (ii) 0.075 m (iii) 5.625
notes.7i: This part of the question was usually well done. Candidates were required to find the friction force and then to use Newton’s Second Law parallel to the plane.
notes.7iii: This part of the question was generally well done. Quite a number of candidates got a =−7.16 but failed to state that the magnitude was 7.16. so they lost the last mark. Answers: (i) v =5 3−1.5−3x (ii) 2.3867 , 4.13 ms–1 (iii) 7.16
notes.key_messages:
Candidates should be reminded that an answer should be given to three significant figures. This means that
they should work to at least four significant figures.
Occasionally candidates use an incorrect formula. A formula booklet is provided so it is recommended that,
when using a formula, they refer to the booklet.
notes.general_comments:
The paper appeared to be the same standard as the one set last November.
Candidates should be reminded of the need for clear presentation in their working, as per the front cover
instructions. The work of a few candidates was rather untidy and sometimes was difficult to read.
Only a handful of candidates gave answers to two significant figures.
It is pleasing to note that most candidates now use g = 10 as requested.
The easier questions proved to be 1, 2, 4(i) and 7(i).
The harder questions proved to be 5(i), 5(ii) and 6(iii).
